ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is marked with latitudes 45°N and 50°N and longitudes 122°E and 125°E, located in a relatively high-latitude area of the Northern Hemisphere. The figure also has boundaries related to frozen soil and labels such as “about 200 days,” indicating that this region has a relatively long number of seasonal frozen-soil days and is close to or has permafrost distributed, which conforms to the “widespread frozen soil” stated in the question stem. Then reason: In high-latitude frozen-soil areas of the Northern Hemisphere, the slope aspects on the two sides of a river valley are different, and the received solar radiation and heating conditions are different, leading to different intensities of freeze-thaw action, slope erosion, and material movement. The development of the valley slopes on the two sides is uneven, so the cross-section of the river valley easily shows the difference of one side being steep and the other side gentle, forming an asymmetric river valley.
